documents.title: Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet V1.0: ASA-CF
Bambu ASA CF Safety Data Sheet SDS20260701B51 (Jul. 01. 2026)
ASA CF / PAHT CF Usage Guide
Filament guide - Printer, Nozzle, AMS, Build Plate, Glue Compatibility and Required Parameters

notes: Independent second extraction (agent-2). No other curated file for this product was read.

Mechanical keys hold the TDS X-Y printed-specimen values (Mechanical Properties, p.2; specimens printed at 275 °C / 90 °C / 200 mm/s / 100% infill and annealed and dried at 80 °C for 12 h before testing, p.3 note). The registry has one key per scope and no *.printed / *.material split, so the Z values are named in each row's note and not stored. Density, melting, Vicat and HDT come from the TDS Physical Properties table and sit under material.* / thermal.*.

TDS facts with no registry key are not stored: Young's modulus (X-Y 4200 ± 270 MPa, Z 2290 ± 260 MPa), melt index (1.74 ± 0.3 g/10 min at 210 °C, 2.16 kg), crystallization temperature ("/"), HDT 102 °C at 1.8 MPa (the 0.45 MPa value is stored), saturated water absorption rate (0.33% at 25 °C, 55% RH), printing and storage humidity (< 20% RH, sealed, with desiccant), retraction length (0.8 - 1.4 mm) and speed (20 - 40 mm/s), max overhang angle (~ 70°), max bridging length (~ 40 mm), spool size (diameter 200 mm, height 67 mm), the X1 Series heatbed drying alternative (90 - 100 °C, 12 h), annealing advice, and the odor, composition, skin hazard, chemical stability, solubility, acid / alkali / solvent / oil resistance, flammability and combustion-product rows.

TDS internal inconsistency (p.3): the Specimen Printing Conditions table says nozzle 220 °C and bed 35 °C, while the footnote under it says the specimens were printed at nozzle 275 °C and bed 90 °C. 220 °C is below the TDS's own recommended nozzle range (250 - 280 °C), so the test_condition cites the footnote. The footnote also gives annealing advice for "Bambu ASA" (80 to 90 °C, 6 to 12 hours), not ASA-CF.

AMS drying, sources disagree: the drying wiki (Appendix I, row "ASA-CF, ABS-GF") gives AMS HT 80 °C for 8 h and AMS 2 Pro "Not compatible"; the ASA-CF wiki (2.1) gives AMS HT 85 °C, 12h. Neither is stored (one drying key pair, holding the TDS oven value).

SDS facts with no registry key are not stored: CLP "Not classified", no hazard pictogram or signal word, physical state "Thread", the section 8 carbon-fibre handling warning (gloves when loading/unloading, cutting or sanding; its text says "carbon fiber-reinforced filament （Glass fiber-reinforced filament)", a wording slip), conditions to avoid (fire, elevated temperatures, direct sunlight), and "Not hazardous goods" for IMDG, DOT, ADR/RID and ICAO-TI / IATA transport. Its section 9 "No data available" does not override the TDS values.

Wiki values that agree with the TDS are recorded as corroboration in the row notes, not as separate rows: flexural strength 72 MPa, impact 14 / 9.4 kJ/m², HDT 110 ℃ at 0.45 MPa, print speed < 250 mm/s, oven drying 80 °C 8 h, heatbed drying 90 - 100 °C 12 h. The ASA-CF wiki comparison table's ASA / PAHT-CF / PPS-CF columns are other products.

Printer guidance: the ASA-CF wiki says "Requires an enclosed printer; not compatible with P1P / A1 series"; the material-table wiki lists enclosed printers (H2 Series, X2D, P2S, X1, X1C, P1S, etc.) for ASA and its CF/GF reinforced materials; the store page says "Enclosure Printers Required". The ASA-CF wiki (2.3) adds that the H2 series and X1E have active chamber heating and that X1C / P1S can preheat the bed for 15 minutes.

Nozzle guidance (ASA-CF wiki 1.3): "0.6 mm nozzle recommended" and "use of 0.4 mm high-flow nozzle is not recommended" are recommendations, not compatibility facts, so they are not written as relations.

Marketing prose proves no number: "67% more stiffness compared to standard ASA", "Superior Outdoor Durability", "Optimized for Large Models" and the page's specimen-size line ("Model size (L*W*H): 220*100*90 mm³") are not stored as values.
No hex: the store page links no hex-code document for this filament and none is cached, so its only colour value "Black (46101)" has no published hex.
No in-the-box list: no official packing list exists for this filament (the store page has no What's in the Box section).

The store page links a "Filament RoHS" certificate (https://store.bblcdn.com/s7/default/a7676855216f4ea2b41e625c8b5a8cac/Bambu_ASA-CF_RoHS.pdf) that was not cached and not read, so safety.certifications is neither curated nor marked not_published.
